purpose: Fixed report fields completed from this independent simulated beginner session and its visible mouse interaction.
persona: Independent simulated first-time RILL beginner interested in a small electronic dance groove; not a human participant.

rating_reasons.easy_to_use: The blank-lane MIDI hint, instrument assignment, pencil note drawing, edge trimming and named File menu actions let me finish with the mouse. Repeating fourteen patterns required many individual clicks.
rating_reasons.how_cool_it_looks: The dark arrangement, turquoise waveforms and clear yellow playback line look polished. Small clip titles became truncated when the whole piece was visible.
rating_reasons.how_fast_it_is: Most editing actions produced prompt visible feedback. WAV export took roughly the piece length in this laboratory session, while MIDI export returned promptly. One file dialog was briefly black before it painted.
rating_reasons.how_confusing_it_is: Only mild confusion: the toolbar Duplicate button selected a tool instead of immediately copying the selected clip. Its visible instruction clarified the next click. The drum and MIDI endpoints were clear on the seconds ruler.
rating_reasons.feature_completeness: The visible workflow covered audio, a VST3 instrument, note editing, duplication, trimming, mouse-entered naming, project save, WAV and MIDI export. The WAV panel exposed an effect-tail option and a fixed-looking 48 kHz stereo 32-bit-float summary; I did not find other format choices in that panel.

findings.observation: Double-clicking the blank lane marked Double-click for MIDI opened the Device library. Assign instrument created a New instrument track and a pattern; the track showed Rill Lab Sine.
Double-clicking the pattern opened a piano roll. Choosing Pencil and making four horizontal mouse drags produced visible C4, C4, E4 and G4 notes and velocity bars.

The context-menu Duplicate command immediately added a pattern. The toolbar Duplicate button instead became highlighted and changed the instruction to Click a clip to duplicate; the copy appeared after the additional clip click.

Zooming out showed the 0:30 ruler mark. Repeated duplicate clicks extended MIDI to 30.000 seconds; duplicating the drum audio and dragging the final audio right edge back aligned both tracks at that endpoint.
At the full-piece zoom, every one-bar MIDI clip title was shortened to New p..., leaving the repeated clips visually similar. I could still see their note marks.

After disabling Loop and pressing Play, the button read Pause, the transport advanced from 001.01.09 to 005.01.37, the yellow playhead moved, and both audio and instrument track meters were illuminated. Stop returned the transport to the beginning.

File > Rename project exposed a Keyboard button. Its on-screen keys and Select all let me enter neon pulse entirely by mouse. Save then suggested neon pulse.rill in the session-2 folder; accepting returned to the arrangement with the unsaved-change dot absent.

Export WAV identified Arrangement 0:30. I unchecked Include effect tails and accepted the suggested neon pulse.wav filename. The status changed from Exporting to Exported. Export MIDI suggested neon pulse.mid and also displayed Exported after accepting.

The first screenshot immediately after opening Export MIDI showed a black rectangle where the native file picker should be. The next screenshot showed the complete usable dialog without further input. This may be specific to the laboratory desktop.

outcome.status: Completed through the visible UI: a 30.000-second arrangement, named and saved project, and successful WAV and MIDI export notices. File contents remain unverified by this participant.
outcome.composition: 112 BPM, 4/4 electronic groove using the supplied Circuit rhythm drum audio repeated across fourteen bars, with the last audio copy trimmed to two bars. Four short C4, C4, E4 and G4 MIDI notes form a one-bar pattern repeated fourteen times alongside the audio.
outcome.playback_observed: Play changed to Pause; transport and yellow playhead advanced across multiple bars; both tracks showed illuminated meters. Stop reset the transport. No audible audition was performed.

limitations: Only the assigned native screenshots and mouse driver were used to interact with the composition. No project or output file contents were inspected; coordinator verification follows.
No audio was auditioned. Visible playback and meters establish UI activity, not sound quality or a verified rendered mix.

This session used a virtual audio sink, software graphics and the supplied Rill Lab Sine. Timing and brief dialog rendering behavior must not be generalized to physical hardware or other VST plug-ins.
The piece is a deliberately simple repeated groove. The task did not require a broader exploration of editing, effects or mixing features.
The screenshot named 21-wav-success.png captures the export in progress; the actual success notice is in 23-wav-exported.png.
